description: Windows Security events related to account sign-in, sign-in failures, authentication protocols, session endings, and account lockouts.

source.inventory_basis: User-supplied Minimal/Common Windows Event ID lists and detailed event catalogue
source.note: Event availability depends on Windows version, audit policy, role, and configuration. Validate provider, channel, event version, and field names against collected event XML.

4610.name: Authentication Package Loaded
4610.title: An authentication component was loaded
4610.description: Windows recorded that an authentication package was loaded by the Local Security Authority.
4610.what_happened: An authentication package became available to Windows for handling authentication requests. This can be part of normal system operation.

who.SubjectUserName: The account associated with the event, if recorded.

where.AuthenticationPackageName: The authentication package that was loaded, if recorded.

4610.when: The time Windows recorded the package load.
4610.why_it_matters: Unexpected authentication packages may deserve review, especially if they are unfamiliar or appear after an unexplained system change.

severity_guidance.low: A known package loads during normal startup or maintenance.
severity_guidance.medium: An unfamiliar package is loaded and its origin needs verification.
severity_guidance.high: An unapproved package is correlated with other suspicious changes.

recommendations: Check whether the package is expected on this device.
Review related system and security changes.
4610.important_note: A package-load event alone does not prove malicious activity.

4611.name: Trusted Logon Process Registered
4611.title: A sign-in component registered with Windows
4611.description: Windows recorded registration of a trusted logon process with the Local Security Authority.
4611.what_happened: A logon process registered so it can participate in Windows authentication.

who.SubjectUserName: The account associated with the event, if recorded.

where.LogonProcessName: The name of the registered logon process, if recorded.

4611.when: The time Windows recorded the registration.
4611.why_it_matters: An unexpected logon process or unusual registration timing may warrant investigation.

severity_guidance.low: The process is known and expected.
severity_guidance.medium: The process is unfamiliar and needs validation.
severity_guidance.high: The registration is unapproved and linked to other suspicious activity.

recommendations: Verify the process name and its expected role.
Review related authentication-package and system events.
4611.important_note: Registration is not, by itself, evidence of compromise.

4622.name: Security Package Loaded
4622.title: A Windows security package was loaded
4622.description: Windows recorded that a security package was loaded by the Local Security Authority.
4622.what_happened: A security package was loaded for use by Windows authentication services.

who.SubjectUserName: The account associated with the event, if recorded.

where.PackageName: The security package name, if recorded.

4622.when: The time Windows recorded the package load.
4622.why_it_matters: Unexpected security packages should be checked against the device's approved configuration.

severity_guidance.low: A known package loads as expected.
severity_guidance.high: An unapproved package is correlated with suspicious system changes.

recommendations: Verify the package name and expected configuration.
Correlate with related authentication and system events.
4622.important_note: A package-load event alone does not prove malicious activity.

4624.name: Successful Logon
4624.title: A sign-in succeeded
4624.description: Windows recorded a successful logon to an account.
4624.what_happened: An account successfully authenticated to Windows and a logon session was created.

who.TargetUserName: The account that successfully signed in.
who.TargetDomainName: The domain or computer associated with the account.
who.SubjectUserName: The account or security context that requested the logon, if recorded.

where.IpAddress: The source IP address, if recorded.
where.WorkstationName: The source computer name, if recorded.
where.LogonType: The type of sign-in, such as interactive, network, service, or Remote Desktop.

4624.when: The date and time Windows recorded the successful logon.
4624.why_it_matters: Successful sign-ins help establish who accessed a device, when, and through which logon method.

severity_guidance.low: The account, device, time, and logon type match expected activity.
severity_guidance.medium: The sign-in is unusual for the account or device and needs review.
severity_guidance.high: The sign-in is correlated with unauthorized access indicators or other confirmed suspicious activity.

recommendations: Check whether the account and sign-in time are expected.
Review unfamiliar source devices, IP addresses, or remote logon types.
Correlate with nearby failed sign-ins and account changes.
4624.important_note: A successful logon is not automatically suspicious. Interpret it using the account, device, logon type, and surrounding activity.

4625.name: Failed Logon
4625.title: Unsuccessful sign-in
4625.description: A sign-in attempt was made, but Windows rejected access to the account.
4625.what_happened: Someone or an application tried to sign in to a Windows account, but authentication failed. This can happen because of an incorrect password, an account restriction, or an expired credential.

who.TargetUserName: The account that someone tried to access.
who.TargetDomainName: The domain or computer associated with the account.

where.IpAddress: The source IP address from which the attempt was recorded, if available.
where.WorkstationName: The computer associated with the login request, if available.
where.LogonType: The type of sign-in attempted, such as local, network or Remote Desktop.

4625.when: The date and time Windows recorded the failed sign-in.
4625.why_it_matters: One failed sign-in is often harmless. Repeated failures, especially from unfamiliar sources, may indicate password guessing or unauthorized access attempts.

severity_guidance.medium: Repeated failed sign-ins against an account.
severity_guidance.high: Repeated failures combined with other suspicious activity.

recommendations: Check whether you recognize the sign-in attempt.
Review repeated failures involving the same account or source.
Investigate unfamiliar remote login activity.
Protect the account if unauthorized access is suspected.
4625.important_note: A failed sign-in does not automatically mean someone hacked the computer.

4634.name: Logoff
4634.title: A sign-in session ended
4634.description: Windows recorded that a logon session was terminated.
4634.what_happened: A previously created Windows logon session ended.

who.TargetUserName: The account associated with the session, if recorded.
who.TargetDomainName: The account domain or computer, if recorded.
who.TargetLogonId: The session identifier used to correlate related events.

where.Computer: The Windows device that recorded the session ending.

4634.when: The time Windows recorded the session termination.
4634.why_it_matters: Logoff events help establish session duration and correlate activity performed during a sign-in.

severity_guidance.medium: The session ending is unexpected and needs context.
severity_guidance.high: The event is part of a correlated sequence indicating possible session misuse.

recommendations: Correlate the Logon ID with the matching successful logon.
Check whether the session ending matches expected user activity.
4634.important_note: This event records session termination; it does not necessarily mean the user manually clicked Sign out.

4647.name: User-Initiated Logoff
4647.title: A user started signing out
4647.description: Windows recorded that a user initiated the logoff process.
4647.what_happened: The user associated with a logon session initiated a sign-out.

who.SubjectUserName: The account that initiated the logoff, if recorded.
who.SubjectDomainName: The domain or computer associated with the account, if recorded.
who.SubjectLogonId: The session identifier used to correlate related events.

where.Computer: The Windows device that recorded the logoff request.

4647.when: The time Windows recorded the user-initiated logoff.
4647.why_it_matters: This helps distinguish a user-initiated sign-out from other session termination events.

severity_guidance.low: The user initiated a normal sign-out.
severity_guidance.medium: The sign-out is unexpected and needs review.
severity_guidance.high: The event is correlated with suspicious session activity.

recommendations: Confirm whether the sign-out was expected.
Correlate the session identifier with related logon and logoff events.
4647.important_note: This event indicates that logoff was initiated; it does not independently explain why.

4648.name: Logon Using Explicit Credentials
4648.title: A program used specified sign-in credentials
4648.description: A process attempted to log on by explicitly supplying account credentials.
4648.what_happened: A user or process supplied credentials different from the credentials of the current logon session, for example when using Run as or accessing a remote resource.

who.SubjectUserName: The account whose session initiated the action, if recorded.
who.TargetUserName: The account whose credentials were supplied.
who.TargetDomainName: The domain associated with the supplied account, if recorded.

where.TargetServerName: The target server or resource, if recorded.
where.ProcessName: The process that attempted to use the explicit credentials, if recorded.
where.IpAddress: The network address associated with the target, if recorded.

4648.when: The time Windows recorded the explicit-credentials logon attempt.
4648.why_it_matters: This can be normal administrative activity, but unexpected use of another account's credentials may need investigation.

severity_guidance.low: The process, account, and target are expected.
severity_guidance.medium: The supplied account or target is unusual.
severity_guidance.high: The event is correlated with credential misuse or unauthorized access.

recommendations: Check whether the initiating user expected this action.
Verify the process and target resource.
Review whether the supplied account is authorized for this task.
4648.important_note: Explicit credential use is not automatically malicious; administrative tools and scheduled tasks may generate it.

4649.name: Replay Attack Detected
4649.title: Windows detected a possible authentication replay
4649.description: Windows recorded a replay-attack detection event.
4649.what_happened: Windows detected authentication information that matched a replay-detection condition.

who.SubjectUserName: The account associated with the event, if recorded.

where.Computer: The Windows device that recorded the event.
where.IpAddress: A related network address, if present in the event data.

4649.when: The time Windows recorded the detection.
4649.why_it_matters: Replay detection is security-relevant and should be investigated with the original event details and surrounding authentication activity.

severity_guidance.low: The event is determined to be a known false positive after review.
severity_guidance.medium: The event is unexplained and requires investigation.
severity_guidance.high: The event is validated and corroborated by related evidence.

recommendations: Review the complete event details and source device.
Correlate with nearby authentication and network events.
Follow the organization's incident response process if validated.
4649.important_note: Preserve the original event and investigate before concluding that an attack succeeded.

4740.name: Account Locked Out
4740.title: A user account was locked
4740.description: Windows recorded that an account became locked out.
4740.what_happened: The account reached a configured lockout condition and Windows locked it.

who.TargetUserName: The account that was locked out.
who.TargetDomainName: The domain or computer associated with the account.

where.CallerComputerName: The computer reported as the source of the lockout request, if recorded.

4740.when: The time Windows recorded the account lockout.
4740.why_it_matters: A lockout can result from repeated incorrect passwords, stale saved credentials, or other authentication problems.

severity_guidance.low: The lockout has a known, expected explanation.
severity_guidance.medium: The source or reason is unclear, or lockouts repeat.
severity_guidance.high: Repeated lockouts are correlated with suspicious authentication attempts.

recommendations: Confirm whether the account owner was trying to sign in.
Check the reported caller computer, if available.
Correlate with failed logons and domain authentication events.
4740.important_note: An account lockout does not by itself prove an attacker caused it.

4768.name: Kerberos Authentication Ticket Requested
4768.title: A Kerberos sign-in ticket was requested
4768.description: A domain controller recorded a request for a Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT).
4768.what_happened: A client requested a Kerberos TGT as part of domain authentication. The event records whether the request succeeded or failed.

who.TargetUserName: The account for which the ticket was requested.
who.ServiceName: The Kerberos service name, if recorded.

where.IpAddress: The client IP address, if recorded.
where.IpPort: The client source port, if recorded.

4768.when: The time the domain controller recorded the ticket request.
4768.why_it_matters: Unexpected ticket requests or unusual failure patterns may help identify domain authentication problems or suspicious activity.

severity_guidance.low: The request matches expected domain sign-in activity.
severity_guidance.medium: The request pattern, account, or source is unusual.
severity_guidance.high: The request is correlated with suspicious Kerberos activity and supporting evidence.

recommendations: Check the account and client address.
Review the result and failure code, if present.
Correlate unusual requests with related Kerberos events.
4768.important_note: A ticket request is a normal part of Kerberos authentication; inspect its result and context.

4769.name: Kerberos Service Ticket Requested
4769.title: Access to a domain service was requested
4769.description: A domain controller recorded a request for a Kerberos service ticket.
4769.what_happened: An account requested a ticket to access a service in a Kerberos domain.

who.TargetUserName: The account requesting the service ticket.
who.ServiceName: The service for which the ticket was requested.

where.IpAddress: The client IP address, if recorded.
where.IpPort: The client source port, if recorded.

4769.when: The time the domain controller recorded the service-ticket request.
4769.why_it_matters: Service-ticket activity helps show which domain services accounts are accessing. Unusual service or account patterns may need review.

severity_guidance.low: The account accesses an expected service.
severity_guidance.medium: The account requests an unusual service ticket.
severity_guidance.high: Unusual ticket activity is correlated with other evidence of account or domain compromise.

recommendations: Verify that the account should access the requested service.
Review unusual service names, client addresses, and request patterns.
Correlate with successful and failed logons.
4769.important_note: A service-ticket request is normal domain activity and is not proof of an attack.

4770.name: Kerberos Service Ticket Renewed
4770.title: A Kerberos service ticket was renewed
4770.description: A domain controller recorded renewal of a Kerberos service ticket.
4770.what_happened: A Kerberos service ticket was renewed so an authenticated session could continue accessing a service.

who.TargetUserName: The account associated with the ticket renewal, if recorded.
who.ServiceName: The service associated with the ticket, if recorded.

where.IpAddress: The client IP address, if recorded.

4770.when: The time the domain controller recorded the renewal.
4770.why_it_matters: Ticket renewals are usually routine, but unusual accounts or service patterns may be worth reviewing.

severity_guidance.low: The renewal matches expected service use.
severity_guidance.medium: The account or service pattern is unusual.
severity_guidance.high: The renewal is part of a correlated suspicious authentication sequence.

recommendations: Verify the account and service are expected.
Review related ticket requests if the renewal is unusual.
4770.important_note: Ticket renewal is a normal Kerberos operation in many environments.

4771.name: Kerberos Pre-Authentication Failed
4771.title: A Kerberos sign-in check failed
4771.description: A domain controller recorded a Kerberos pre-authentication failure.
4771.what_happened: A Kerberos authentication request failed during its pre-authentication check.

who.TargetUserName: The account involved in the Kerberos request, if recorded.

where.IpAddress: The client IP address, if recorded.
where.IpPort: The client source port, if recorded.

4771.when: The time the domain controller recorded the failure.
4771.why_it_matters: Repeated failures or unfamiliar sources may indicate incorrect credentials, configuration problems, or suspicious authentication attempts.

severity_guidance.low: An isolated failure with a known explanation.
severity_guidance.medium: Repeated failures against an account or from a source.
severity_guidance.high: Failures are correlated with other suspicious authentication evidence.

recommendations: Review the failure code and account involved.
Check whether the source device is recognized.
Correlate repeated failures with 4768 and 4625 events.
4771.important_note: A pre-authentication failure does not by itself prove password spraying or an attack.

4772.name: Kerberos Authentication Ticket Request Failed
4772.title: A Kerberos ticket request failed
4772.description: Windows recorded a failed Kerberos authentication ticket request.
4772.what_happened: A Kerberos ticket request was not completed successfully. The event's result or failure information should be used to understand why.

who.TargetUserName: The account involved in the request, if recorded.

where.IpAddress: The client IP address, if recorded.

4772.when: The time Windows recorded the failed request.
4772.why_it_matters: Repeated or unexplained failures may indicate credential, configuration, or domain authentication problems.

severity_guidance.low: An isolated failure with a known explanation.
severity_guidance.medium: Repeated or unexplained failures need review.
severity_guidance.high: The failures are correlated with other suspicious authentication evidence.

recommendations: Inspect the complete event and failure information.
Check the account and source device.
Correlate with other Kerberos events.
4772.important_note: Use the actual event provider and event version to confirm the event meaning and available fields before parsing.

4774.name: Account Mapped for Logon
4774.title: An account was mapped for sign-in
4774.description: Windows recorded that an account was mapped for logon.
4774.what_happened: An account-mapping operation occurred as part of an authentication process.

who.TargetUserName: The account that was mapped, if recorded.

where.Computer: The computer that recorded the account-mapping event.

4774.when: The time Windows recorded the mapping.
4774.why_it_matters: Unexpected account mapping may need review in environments that use mapped or external accounts.

severity_guidance.high: The mapping is unapproved and linked to suspicious access.

recommendations: Verify the account and mapping configuration.
Review related authentication events.
4774.important_note: An account-mapping event alone does not establish unauthorized access.

4775.name: Account Could Not Be Mapped for Logon
4775.title: Windows could not map an account for sign-in
4775.description: Windows recorded that an account could not be mapped for logon.
4775.what_happened: An authentication process attempted to map an account, but the mapping did not succeed.

where.Computer: The computer that recorded the mapping failure.

4775.when: The time Windows recorded the mapping failure.
4775.why_it_matters: This may indicate an account configuration or authentication mapping problem. Repeated unexplained failures deserve review.

severity_guidance.low: A known configuration issue explains the event.
severity_guidance.medium: The mapping failure is unexplained or recurring.
severity_guidance.high: The failure is correlated with suspicious authentication activity.

recommendations: Check the account and mapping configuration.
Review related authentication failures and domain events.
4775.important_note: A mapping failure is not proof of an attack.

4776.name: NTLM Credentials Validated
4776.title: Windows checked NTLM sign-in credentials
4776.description: A computer recorded validation of account credentials using NTLM authentication.
4776.what_happened: Windows attempted to validate credentials through NTLM. The event result indicates whether validation succeeded.

who.TargetUserName: The account whose credentials were checked.

where.Workstation: The workstation from which the validation request was received, if recorded.

4776.when: The time Windows recorded the credential validation.
4776.why_it_matters: NTLM validation may be expected in some environments, but unexpected use or repeated failures can indicate legacy authentication or suspicious activity.

severity_guidance.low: NTLM use is expected and the validation succeeds.
severity_guidance.medium: NTLM use is unexpected or validation repeatedly fails.
severity_guidance.high: NTLM activity is correlated with suspicious account or network behavior.

recommendations: Check whether NTLM is expected for this account and device.
Review the validation result and source workstation.
Correlate failures with 4625 and 4771 events.
4776.important_note: This event records credential validation; it does not always identify the final resource accessed.

4777.name: NTLM Credentials Validation Failed
4777.title: NTLM sign-in credentials could not be validated
4777.description: A computer recorded a failed NTLM credential validation.
4777.what_happened: Windows could not validate the supplied credentials through NTLM.

who.TargetUserName: The account whose credentials were checked, if recorded.

where.Workstation: The workstation associated with the validation request, if recorded.

4777.when: The time Windows recorded the failed validation.
4777.why_it_matters: Repeated failures or unexpected NTLM use may indicate incorrect saved credentials, configuration issues, or suspicious authentication activity.

severity_guidance.low: An isolated failure has a known explanation.
severity_guidance.medium: Failures repeat or originate from an unfamiliar workstation.
severity_guidance.high: Failures are correlated with other suspicious authentication events.

recommendations: Check the account and source workstation.
Review NTLM configuration and the failure details.
Correlate with 4625 and 4776 events.
4777.important_note: A failed NTLM validation does not by itself prove an attack.

implementation_notes.severity_note: Use event frequency, account importance, source familiarity, logon type, result codes, asset context, and correlated evidence. Do not assign a threat verdict from Event ID alone.
implementation_notes.parser_note: Map fields from the actual provider payload and event version. Do not assume every listed field exists in every Windows version or event variant.
